strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine gap: extends human-AI collaboration from discrete (Overcooked-AI) to continuous, physics-based environments
Comprehensive benchmark design with 12 diverse maps across three collaboration modes (coordination, awareness, action consistency) and two complementary evaluation tasks
Solid experimental methodology: multiple baselines, AI-AI and human-AI evaluation, ablation studies, user study with 32 participants, and honest limitations discussion
Useful community resource: 1,000+ human-human demonstrations, 720 expert demonstrations with randomized properties, promised code release, and detailed reproducibility information
Consistent empirical improvements validated across metrics and demonstrated with human participants (statistically significant improvement in helpfulness, p=0.017)
Strong experimental practices including failure case analysis and comparison with oracle simulator as upper bound
weaknesses: Critical unresolved technical issue: sub-trajectory recombination validity is acknowledged but not addressed. No analysis of how many generated trajectories violate physical constraints, undermining a core contribution of BASS

Concerning dynamics model performance: 48.7% prediction accuracy on Task 2 (vs 62.5% on Task 1) raises questions about whether the model adequately captures physical constraints when generalizing to unseen attributes

BASS methodology is somewhat incremental: behavior augmentation via pose perturbation is straightforward, dynamics-based action selection builds on acknowledged prior work, and partner action prediction simply reuses the learned policy by state swapping

Weak RL baseline: MAPPO struggles due to continuous space complexity, leaving no competitive RL baseline and making it difficult to assess whether improvements are due to BASS or simply the advantage of behavior cloning with rich data

Limited generalization analysis: no cross-task evaluation (Task 1→Task 2 transfer), evaluation still restricted to 12 maps with only varied object properties, and 'unseen' attributes limited to shape/size/mass variations
Action selection uses only Normalized Final Distance as reward, ignoring other important metrics (waiting time, action consistency) that could enable more sophisticated multi-objective selection
Sub-trajectory matching relies on heuristic discretization (48×48 grid) without justification, and the method's sensitivity to this hyperparameter is unexplored

Limited human validation: only 12 participants actually played against models; 32 total participants with modest per-participant trials; no analysis of whether rated behaviors correspond to actual human-like play
Incomplete statistical analysis: significance testing reported only for helpfulness metric; other results lack formal significance tests despite showing modest differences

strengths: Addresses genuine gap in human-AI collaboration research: most prior work (Overcooked-AI, Hanabi) uses discrete symbolic spaces, while this work tackles continuous control with realistic physics constraints
Well-designed benchmark with thoughtfully organized 12 maps by collaboration mode and two complementary evaluation tasks targeting different generalization challenges
Comprehensive human dataset (>1,000 demonstrations from 36 participants for Task 1) with quantitative diversity validation showing superior coverage vs. expert/RL baselines
Rigorous experimental evaluation combining AI-AI and human-AI testing with multiple baselines (MLP, GRU, DP, MAPPO) and appropriate metrics (TCR, NFD, WT, AC) with ablations
Sophisticated evaluation protocols addressing reproducibility concerns (cross-group evaluation for Task 1, compositional generalization for Task 2)
Extensive implementation details in appendices support reproducibility; inference speed analyzed for real-time feasibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: BASS combines standard techniques (Gaussian noise augmentation, trajectory recombination, latent dynamics models, action selection) without significant algorithmic innovation; multi-agent augmentation extension is incremental

Large performance gap between AI-AI evaluation (Table 2, main results) and human-AI play (cross-group DP: 0.3233→0.3855, DP/BASS: 0.3503→0.6512) raises concerns about whether cross-group protocol truly captures human behavior diversity and ecological validity
Failure rates remain substantial after BASS improvement: {0.797, 0.688, 0.906} to {0.343, 0.563, 0.484}; paper acknowledges limitations remain 'a substantial challenge'
Severely limited scope: single 2D physics domain with only 12 maps; only tested on one additional environment (Overcooked-AI, +15% improvement) with no 3D or robotics validation

Dynamics model and partner prediction underspecified: extremely simple 2-layer MLP architecture (128 units, 32-dim latent) with no ablation on choices; partner action prediction only ~71% accurate but impact on performance unclear

MAPPO baseline appears disadvantaged compared to BC methods despite being standard MARL algorithm; poor RL performance (often worse than MLP) suggests either mismatched task design or unfair comparison, weakening baseline strength

Significant AI-AI to human-AI gap (69% TCR improvement for DP/BASS) undermines whether cross-group evaluation (Table 2 primary results) is valid proxy for human adaptation; Task 2 entirely lacks human evaluation
Dataset quality concerns: Task 1 has highly variable participant contribution (3-5 to 72 demos); Task 2 uses only 4 expert players limiting diversity; no inter-annotator reliability study
Statistical rigor issues: no significance testing for main results despite marginal improvements on some metrics (AC: 0.8337 vs 0.8163, <1% difference)
Key design choices relegated to appendices rather than main text (e.g., 4 action candidates justified in Appendix K); project page URL mentioned in abstract but not provided
